summary.title: Meaningful Availability
summary.one_liner: A research paper introducing windowed user-uptime, a cloud availability metric that models user-perceived availability and distinguishes many short outages from fewer long ones.
takeaways: Traditional availability metrics can be biased and may not reflect what users actually experience.
Windowed user-uptime models user-perceived availability by computing availability over many windows at once.
The metric distinguishes many short periods of unavailability from fewer, longer ones.
The approach is evaluated in the context of Google's G Suite.
summary.summary: The paper argues that high availability matters for cloud applications and that a good availability metric helps both users set expectations and developers know what to improve. It proposes windowed user-uptime, evaluated on Google's G Suite. The metric directly models user-perceived availability, which the authors say avoids bias in common availability metrics. It computes availability across many windows simultaneously, so it can tell apart many short outages from fewer longer ones. The page is the NSDI '20 paper abstract with citation details; the full text is behind the linked presentation page.
